summary:
LUNA-OPS: Build Your Own Lunar Colony is an interactive browser-based lunar colony simulation developed by Team OORT for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge, Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.

Designed for children aged 7–12, the game places players in charge of establishing and managing a lunar outpost over a 30-day mission. Players construct habitats, solar panels, greenhouses, ice drills, storm shelters and communication facilities while managing electricity, oxygen, water, food and astronaut health.

Through interactive astronauts, rover exploration, radio missions, resource management and simulated solar storm events, players experience the challenges of sustaining human life beyond Earth.

LUNA-OPS transforms complex space exploration concepts into an accessible educational experience, encouraging curiosity about lunar science, engineering, sustainability and the future of human space exploration.
details:
LUNA-OPS is an interactive lunar colony-building and survival simulation that introduces young players to the challenges of establishing a sustainable human presence on the Moon.

The mission begins with a spacecraft landing and a crew of astronauts arriving on the lunar surface. Players must establish a functioning outpost and keep their astronauts safe throughout a 30-day mission.

The game features an interactive isometric lunar map where players can inspect terrain and construct six types of facilities: Moon Homes, Solar Panels, Greenhouses, Ice Drills, Storm Safe Rooms and Radio Dishes.

Players manage electricity, oxygen, water, food, building materials and astronaut health. Each mission day updates resource production and consumption, allowing players to understand the consequences of their decisions.

Additional features include animated astronauts, rover exploration, radio missions, educational messages, resource warnings, a solar storm forecast and a storm survival challenge. Players must plan ahead, balance limited resources and protect their crew.

The project is designed for children aged 7–12. Its goal is to make lunar exploration more accessible by turning complex scientific and engineering concepts into interactive learning experiences.

LUNA-OPS was developed using Phaser 3, JavaScript, HTML and CSS, with Visual Studio Code as the development environment. AI-assisted tools were used during development for coding support, debugging and the creation of certain audio and visual effects.

The project combines simulation, storytelling and educational gameplay to encourage curiosity about space exploration, engineering, sustainability and the future of human settlement beyond Earth.
